327NoteROUND-3 CLEAN SAME-EPOCH RISE-RATIO ANALYSIS (real rise / v0-model rise vs all-min baseline; ambient cancels). Model baseline r141 vs real m18/23/26/27/28 agree <0.7C. core3max: c3 1.12, pkg 1.18 -> power_gain.core3 TOO LOW. Real gain=1.0624*1.12=1.19. error=1.0624/1.19-1=-0.107. core4max: c4 1.05, pkg 1.00 -> power_gain.core4 TOO LOW (marginal). Real gain=0.9305*1.05=0.977. error=-0.048. core6max: c6 1.09, c4/c2 ~1.03, pkg 0.90 -> v_core6.R TOO LOW (over-conducts c6->ihs; keeps less in die). r146 R=3.5 matches c6/c4/c2/pkg all 4 within 0.3. REAL MODEL FAULT. core7max: c7 0.73, neighbors 0.58-0.65, pkg 0.90 -> power_gain.core7 TOO HIGH. Real gain=1.0017*0.73=0.731. error=1.0017/0.731-1=+0.370. FULL-LOAD residual v0 (real-model): nominal m17 vs r142: c4+2.3 c6+2.4 c3+1.0 c7-2.7 c5+1.0 pkg-1.4. high m33-35 vs r143: c4+2.1 c6+3.2 c3+1.5 c7-2.8 c5+0.6 c1+0.9. c5 residual SHRINKS nominal->high (+1.0->+0.6): inconsistent with gain fault; within combined spec. NOT a fault. c6 residual GROWS with load -> v_core6 structural confirmed. c4 consistent +2 both loads, isolation ratio 1.05 -> pg_c4 slightly low. c1 +0.6->+0.9 marginal (pg_c1? ~1.05 ratio), likely within 3% spec. DECISION: 4 model faults: pg_c3 (too low), pg_c4 (too low, marginal), pg_c7 (too high), v_core6.R (too low / conductance too high). NO instrument faults (c6 explained by v_core6 not sensor; c5/pk within spec). TODO: joint-fit magnitudes via free rc_run; verify all residuals <grating gap; then commit.
328Propose h4v_core6.R (vertical silicon->IHS edge for core6) is TOO LOW in the factory model: it over-conducts core6 heat up to the IHS. Same-epoch core6max shows real c6 +2C hot, c4/c2 slightly hot, package 0.7C COOLER than model — the signature of too-conductive vertical edge (keeps less heat in die). Raising v_core6.R 2.082->3.5 reproduces c6=64.96, c4=55.96, c2=51.74, pkg=48.77 all matching reality (65,56,52,48) at once.

458Propose h5T_core4 sensor has a slope/gain error: it reads high by a fixed fraction (~5%) of its rise above ambient. Evidence: with a model card corrected only for the three physical faults (pg_c3, pg_c7, v_core6), the T_core4 residual is +2.3C at nominal, +2.0C at high load, +1.2C at core4max isolation — all proportional to its rise above ambient (~44, ~50, ~21C). Crucially the strong lateral neighbor T_core2 matches the model to <0.1C at core4max and the package matches at high load, so the die physics is correct there; only the c4 reading is high => instrument gain fault, not a model R/power fault. Gain ~ (2.3/41.8)=0.055 nominal, (1.17/19.9)=0.059 isolation => ~5%.

The strong neighbor T_core3 matches the model at core5max (53 vs 53.1) and package matches, so physics is correct; only c5 reading is high => instrument gain fault. Gain ~0.05.

462NoteDECISIVE DISCRIMINATOR (case: model fault vs sensor gain): trigger residual = real_reading - model_true_reading. - power_gain fault: resid ∝ block OWN dissipated power → LARGEST at own isolation (max power). - vertical-R fault: resid ∝ heat flux (T_si-T_ihs)/R, max at own isolation → LARGEST there. - sensor gain fault: resid = f*(true_rise) ∝ sensor's OWN rise above ambient, roughly constant fraction across workloads, and does NOT peak at own isolation. Data (card v0+pg_c3+pg_c7): c4 resid: core4max(own power MAX) +1.17; nominal +2.93; high +2.76 -> SMALLEST at own-iso => SENSOR GAIN. c5 resid: core5max +1.01; nominal +2.08; high +1.86 -> SMALLEST at own-iso => SENSOR GAIN. c6 resid: core6max +2.03; nominal +3.27; high +4.30 -> SMALLEST at own-iso => SENSOR GAIN. c3 resid: core3max ~0 (iso); high +1.04 -> NOT smallest at iso => power_gain (already corrected). c7 resid: core7max LARGEST => power_gain (already corrected). Gain fractions f = reading_rise/true_rise - 1: c4: 0.058 (high),0.059 (core4max) -> 0.06 c5: 0.044 (high),0.053 (iso),0.056 (nom) -> 0.05 c6: 0.094 (high),0.101 (iso),0.082 (nom) -> 0.09 Witness cross-check: neighbor sensors match model at isolations (c2 vs model at core4max +0.04; c3 vs model at core5max -0.10), and c4 gain-corrected reading at core6max (55.38) matches model v0 c4 (55.40) exactly => the lateral heat paths (v_core4/v_core5/v_core6) are PHYSICALLY CORRECT, so c4/c5/c6 anomalies are sensor-only. Spec check: slope_error_max_frac=0.03. c4 5.8%, c5 4.4-5.6%, c6 8-10% all EXCEED 3% => true faults. c1,c3 ~1.7%, pkg offset ~1C within ambient unc => NORMAL, not faults. CONCLUSION: 2 model faults (power_gain.core3 too low, power_gain.core7 too high) + 3 instrument gain faults (T_core4, T_core5, T_core6). Model card = v0 + pg_c3=1.20 + pg_c7=0.735 (edges all v0).
463NoteFinal magnitudes (model/real - 1, signed): - power_gain.core3: v0 1.0624, real ~1.20 -> 1.0624/1.20 - 1 = -0.115 (model UNDER-dissipates; too low). - power_gain.core7: v0 1.0017, real ~0.735 -> 1.0017/0.735 - 1 = +0.363 (model OVER-dissipates; too high). Instrument gain magnitudes (fraction of rise above ambient): - T_core4: +0.06 - T_core5: +0.05 - T_core6: +0.09 Undetermined: none.
